title: Singer Madeleine Maitland Green, Benny Goodman and Earl Hines
summary: They hire a pretty singer, Chester Lane writes for her, Benny Goodman briefly takes her and she goes on to Earl Hines.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: That's right, that's right. You're right. Anyway, we first had an engagement in Cincinnati, came on back to St. Louis and we got ready, you know what I mean, for the opening season --
Madeleine Maitland Green was in that, too.
Oh, yeah, we picked up a girl named Madeleine Maitland Green. You ever hear of her?

She was a singer, a very pretty girl. One of the most beautiful girls you ever seen in your life. Beautiful complexion, pretty eyes, and had a nice little poise. Benny Goodman came through here and he heard her and he kind of liked her. So we said, "Well, take her, Benny, because you can do more for her than we can ever do for her," see. And so we turned her loose and Benny took her, but she didn't last long. I think she stayed with him two or three weeks.

She went and joined Earl Hines' band. We heard her in Cincinnati, brought her back to St. Louis, had Chester Lane to write You Go To My Head, made several arrangements behind her. We took her downtown to a wholesale house where she could buy four or five little evening dresses. They were cheap. But things were rough back in those days. People weren't wearing $100 dresses back in those days. And this was a wholesale place, and she was -- she got to be a Miss Any. (Unintelligible) She was real popular. People were coming in and requesting songs for her to sing and whatnot.
Then she started making a little money on the intermissions.
Yeah. Then she got so that -- I'd call a song, and she'd -- I don't want to sing that." So one night I had to read the riot act on her, and put her in her
place. You have to do that once in a while, you know. So we got along. Told her, 'Don't be Miss Ann on us now. We're all here scuffling together.'
